subtopics.title: Distribution and Density — Two Different Ideas

questions.question: Population distribution refers to:
options: The average number of people per square kilometre
The pattern of where people are spread across an area
The rate at which a population is growing
The number of births per thousand people

questions.question: Two districts each have 50 000 people in 1 000 km². In one they are spread evenly; in the other all live in a single town. This shows that:
options: The densities must be different
Distribution and density mean the same thing
Density cannot be calculated for either district
Identical density can go with completely different distribution

questions.question: Settlement strung out along a river or main road is described as:
options: Linear
Clustered
Dispersed
Uninhabited

questions.question: "Sparsely populated" means:
options: Nobody lives there at all
Few people spread over a large area
Many people in a small area
The population is growing slowly

subtopics.title: Calculating Density — and What It Hides

questions.question: A municipality has 240 000 people and covers 1 600 km². Its population density is:
options: 384 000 people per km²
1 500 people per km²
150 people per km²
15 people per km²

questions.question: Gauteng occupies under 2% of South Africa's area but holds about a quarter of its people. This gives Gauteng a density of:
options: About 3 people per km²
About 50 people per km²
About 150 people per km²
Well above 800 people per km²

questions.question: The main weakness of a national population density figure is that:
options: It is an average that conceals huge internal variation, describing no actual place
It uses the wrong units
It cannot be calculated for large countries
It changes every day

questions.question: Geographers sometimes divide population by ARABLE land rather than total land because:
options: Arable land is easier to measure
It shows how many people each unit of productive land must support, which total area hides
It always gives a smaller number
Total area is not recorded by governments

questions.question: Which is the STRONGEST single physical control on where people live?
options: Vegetation type
Soil colour
Climate, especially temperature and reliable rainfall
Distance from the equator

questions.question: Equatorial rainforests are sparsely populated mainly because of:
options: Extreme cold and a frozen growing season
A complete absence of fresh water
Constant earthquakes
Leached soils, dense vegetation and disease

questions.question: Mineral deposits attract dense population even to unattractive sites because:
options: The resource cannot be moved to the people, so the people must come to it
Mines always improve the climate
Mining areas have the best soils
Governments require people to live there

questions.question: Some of the densest rural populations on earth are found on floodplains and deltas because of:
options: Their high altitude
Deep, fertile alluvial soils that support intensive agriculture
Their distance from rivers
Their cold winters

subtopics.title: Human Factors and South Africa's Pattern

questions.question: South Africa's population is much denser in the east than the west chiefly because:
options: The east is closer to the equator
The west has no minerals
Rainfall declines westward, falling below about 500 mm a year over much of the west
The east has flatter land

questions.question: Gauteng is described as an anomaly in the population pattern because it:
options: Has the highest rainfall in the country
Is the largest province by area
Lies on the coast with the country's best harbour
Has no coast and no navigable river, yet holds the largest concentration of people — because of gold

questions.question: High rural population densities in parts of the Eastern Cape and Limpopo are best explained by:
options: Apartheid-era policy that confined the majority population to a small share of the land in the homelands
Exceptionally fertile volcanic soils
The presence of major ports
Very high rainfall totals

questions.question: The recommended order for answering a question about a population pattern is:
options: Explanation, then evidence, then pattern
Pattern first, then the evidence for it, then the explanation
Calculation only
List every factor alphabetically

questions.question: Moving forty learners from a classroom into a stadium changes:
options: The population size
The birth rate
The density, because the same number of people now occupies far more space
Nothing at all

questions.question: Gathering the same forty people into one corner of the stadium changes:
options: The density but not the distribution
Neither density nor distribution
Both density and distribution
The distribution but not the density

questions.question: A question asking about DISTRIBUTION should be answered with:
options: Words describing the pattern — clustered, linear, dense here, empty there
A single figure in people per square kilometre
A birth rate per thousand
The total area in square kilometres

subtopics.title: Why Nobody Builds a City in the Kalahari

questions.question: In dry country, settlement often forms a thin string of dots because:
options: The government builds only along straight lines
Settlement follows the watercourse, since fresh water is the first requirement
The soil is only fertile in strips
Roads are cheaper to build in a line

questions.question: Steep mountain areas hold few people mainly because of:
options: Excessive rainfall
The absence of minerals
Thin soils, difficult access and expensive building
Extremely fertile land being protected

questions.question: A natural harbour attracts dense settlement because:
options: It improves the local climate
It supplies drinking water
It provides fertile soil
Trade collects there, and people collect around trade

questions.question: Drawing an imaginary line down the middle of South Africa shows that:
options: The east receives decent rain and holds most of the people, while the west is dry and sparsely settled
The west receives more rain than the east
Population is evenly spread on both sides
All settlement is coastal

questions.question: The chain of growth described for Gauteng runs:
options: Harbour, trade, factories, mines
Gold, mine workers, towns and services, factories making machinery, banks and offices, roads and railways
Farming, rainfall, dams, cities
Government offices, schools, mines, gold

questions.question: Gauteng remains the economic heart of the region even though the gold is largely worked out because:
options: The gold reserves are secretly untouched
The climate has improved
Once people, roads and jobs are established in a place, they hold each other there
Government forbids people to leave

questions.question: Durban, Cape Town and Gqeberha all grew large chiefly because:
options: They have the highest rainfall
They sit on gold reefs
They are the flattest sites in the country
Harbours bring trade, trade brings factories, and factories bring jobs

questions.question: The three-point summary of South Africa's population map given in the lesson is:
options: Dense east and empty dry west from rainfall; four city clusters from gold and harbours; crowded rural pockets in the former homelands from history
Even spread; low density; no cities
Coastal only; inland empty; no rural population
Dense west, empty east, and no urban centres
